open_obligations: Note that soundness is only against limited optimisation in Kirchner et al.
Check the thresholds used for 'high' recall and 'low' false-positive rate.
Check that adversarial provers come from the same model family.
in.other_title: Legibility: relaxed completeness for the helpful prover and soundness against adversarial inputs
in.rationale: Anil et al. define the desired protocol by perfect recall (completeness) and perfect precision (soundness). Kirchner et al. relax these to a high helpful-prover pass rate with high verifier recall, and a low false-positive rate on adversarial inputs from limited optimisation, calling the helpful prover legible to the verifier when both hold.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: completeness and soundness criteria for prover-verifier protocols, relaxed for informal domains

text: The authors define a desirable verification protocol by two properties: possibility of perfect recall (some prover can help the verifier reach zero false negatives, linked to completeness) and guarantee of perfect precision (no prover can trick the verifier into a false positive, linked to soundness). They set incentives so the verifier is rewarded for the correct answer and the prover for getting the verifier to answer 'yes' regardless of the correct answer, making the game collaborative on yes-instances and adversarial on no-instances.
title: PVG desiderata: perfect recall (completeness), perfect precision (soundness); incentives
